333	def _check_cells(index, cells, nx, ny):
334	    if not isinstance(cells, tuple):
335	        raise TypeError(f"layers[{index}].cells must be a tuple")
336	    if len(cells) != nx * ny:
337	        raise ValueError(
338	            f"layers[{index}].cells must have nx * ny elements"
339	        )
340	    for j in range(len(cells)):
341	        prefix = f"layers[{index}].cells[{j}]: "
342	        cell = cells[j]
343	        if not isinstance(cell, tuple):
344	            raise TypeError(prefix + "must be a tuple")
345	        if len(cell) != 2:
346	            raise ValueError(prefix + "must have 2 elements")
347	        count, mean = cell
348	        if type(count) is not int:
349	            raise TypeError(prefix + "count must be a non-bool int")
350	        if not count >= 0:
351	            raise ValueError(prefix + "count must be >= 0")
352	        if count == 0:
353	            if mean is not None:
354	                raise ValueError(prefix + "mean must be None when count is 0")
355	        else:
356	            if type(mean) is not float:
357	                raise TypeError(prefix + "mean must be a float")
358	            if not math.isfinite(mean):
359	                raise ValueError(prefix + "mean must be finite")
360	            if not mean >= 0:
361	                raise ValueError(prefix + "mean must be >= 0")
362	
363	
364	def _check_analysis(index, analysis, nx, ny):
365	    if not isinstance(analysis, tuple):
366	        raise TypeError(f"layers[{index}].analysis must be a tuple")
367	    if len(analysis) != nx * ny:
368	        raise ValueError(
369	            f"layers[{index}].analysis must have nx * ny elements"
370	        )
371	    for j in range(len(analysis)):
372	        prefix = f"layers[{index}].analysis[{j}]: "
373	        cell = analysis[j]
374	        if not isinstance(cell, tuple):
375	            raise TypeError(prefix + "must be a tuple")
376	        if len(cell) != 2:
377	            raise ValueError(prefix + "must have 2 elements")
378	        slope, roughness = cell
379	        if slope is not None:
380	            if type(slope) is not float:
381	                raise TypeError(prefix + "slope must be a float")
382	            if not math.isfinite(slope):
383	                raise ValueError(prefix + "slope must be finite")
384	            if not slope >= 0:
385	                raise ValueError(prefix + "slope must be >= 0")
386	        if roughness is None:
387	            if slope is not None:
388	                raise ValueError(
389	                    prefix
390	                    + "roughness must not be None when slope is not None"
391	                )
392	        else:
393	            if type(roughness) is not float:
394	                raise TypeError(prefix + "roughness must be a float")
395	            if not math.isfinite(roughness):
396	                raise ValueError(prefix + "roughness must be finite")
397	            if not roughness >= 0:
398	                raise ValueError(prefix + "roughness must be >= 0")

401	def _check_quality(index, item):
402	    prefix = f"layers[{index}].quality: "
403	    if not isinstance(item, dict):
404	        raise TypeError(prefix + "must be a dict")
405	    if list(item.keys()) != list(_QUALITY_KEYS):
406	        raise TypeError(
407	            prefix
408	            + "keys must be in the order resolution, total, valid, "
409	            "coverage, slope_exceed, roughness_exceed"
410	        )
411	
412	    resolution = item["resolution"]
413	    if type(resolution) is not float:
414	        raise TypeError(prefix + "resolution must be a float")
415	    if not math.isfinite(resolution):
416	        raise ValueError(prefix + "resolution must be finite")
417	    if resolution < 0:
418	        raise ValueError(prefix + "resolution must be >= 0")
419	
420	    total = item["total"]
421	    if type(total) is not int:
422	        raise TypeError(prefix + "total must be a non-bool int")
423	    if not total > 0:
424	        raise ValueError(prefix + "total must be > 0")
425	
426	    valid = item["valid"]
427	    if type(valid) is not int:
428	        raise TypeError(prefix + "valid must be a non-bool int")
429	    if not 0 <= valid <= total:
430	        raise ValueError(prefix + "valid must be in [0, total]")
431	
432	    coverage = item["coverage"]
433	    if type(coverage) is not float:
434	        raise TypeError(prefix + "coverage must be a float")
435	    if not math.isfinite(coverage):
436	        raise ValueError(prefix + "coverage must be finite")
437	    if not 0 <= coverage <= 1:
438	        raise ValueError(prefix + "coverage must be in [0, 1]")
439	
440	    for name in ("slope_exceed", "roughness_exceed"):
441	        value = item[name]
442	        if type(value) is not int:
443	            raise TypeError(prefix + f"{name} must be a non-bool int")
444	        if not 0 <= value <= total:
445	            raise ValueError(prefix + f"{name} must be in [0, total]")
446

455	        )

457	    resolution = item["resolution"]

560	def serialize(product):
561	    """Serialize a :func:`build` result dict to UTF-8 JSON bytes.
562	
563	    ``product`` must be the dict returned by :func:`build`, with keys
564	    exactly in the order ``crosspoint, layers, overall``:
565	    ``crosspoint`` is the dict returned by
566	    :func:`ocean_sonar.crosspoint.evaluate` (keys
567	    ``count, bias, rmse, max_abs, within_tolerance, quality``) with
568	    ``count`` a positive non-bool int, ``within_tolerance`` a non-bool
569	    int in ``[0, count]``, ``bias``/``rmse``/``max_abs`` finite floats
570	    (the latter two ``>= 0``) and ``quality`` equal to ``"pass"``
571	    exactly when ``within_tolerance == count`` and to ``"fail"``
572	    exactly when ``within_tolerance < count``;
573	    ``layers`` is a non-empty tuple with one dict per resolution and
574	    ``overall`` is ``"pass"`` or ``"fail"``. Each layer dict has keys
575	    exactly in the order
576	    ``resolution, nx, ny, cells, analysis, quality, substrate``:
577	    ``resolution`` a finite float ``> 0``; ``nx``/``ny`` non-bool
578	    positive ints; ``cells`` and ``analysis`` tuples of length
579	    ``nx * ny`` whose items are the ``(count, mean)`` and
580	    ``(slope, roughness)`` tuples produced by
581	    :func:`ocean_sonar.grid.build` and
582	    :func:`ocean_sonar.terrain.analyze` — empty cells are
583	    ``(0, None)``/``(None, None)`` and boundary cells may also be
584	    ``(None, roughness)`` —; ``quality`` and ``substrate`` are
585	    the matching items returned by :func:`ocean_sonar.quality.assess`
586	    and :func:`ocean_sonar.substrate.classify`. ``overall`` is
587	    recomputed with the :func:`ocean_sonar.report.summarize` rule from
588	    ``crosspoint`` and the per-layer ``quality``/``substrate`` values.
589	
590	    Validation order, stopping at the first error: the top-level
591	    container and key order, then ``crosspoint``, then the layers tuple
592	    and each layer in index order — per layer its container, key order
593	    and ``resolution``/``nx``/``ny``, then ``cells``, then
594	    ``analysis``, then ``quality``, then ``substrate`` — and finally
595	    ``overall``. Container, key-order and field-type errors raise
596	    ``TypeError``; length, finiteness, range, consistency and enum
597	    errors (including an ``overall`` that disagrees with the recomputed
598	    verdict) raise ``ValueError``. The input is not modified.
599	
600	    On success the product is encoded as UTF-8 JSON with the key order
601	    preserved, ``ensure_ascii=False``, ``separators=(",", ":")``,
602	    ``allow_nan=False``, no indentation and no trailing newline.
603	    Floats are first rounded with ``round(float(v), 6)`` and negative
604	    zero is normalized to ``0.0``; tuples are recursively converted to
605	    arrays. Any JSON or UTF-8 encoding failure raises ``ValueError``.
606	
607	    Returns the JSON document as ``bytes``.
608	    """
609	    if not isinstance(product, dict):
610	        raise TypeError("product must be a dict")
611	    if list(product.keys()) != list(_PRODUCT_KEYS):
612	        raise TypeError(
613	            "product keys must be in the order crosspoint, layers, overall"
614	        )
615	
616	    crosspoint_result = product["crosspoint"]
617	    layers = product["layers"]
618	    _check_product_crosspoint(crosspoint_result)
619	
620	    if not isinstance(layers, tuple):
621	        raise TypeError("layers must be a tuple")
622	    if len(layers) == 0:
623	        raise ValueError("layers must be non-empty")
624	
625	    for i in range(len(layers)):
626	        _check_layer(i, layers[i])
627	
628	    overall = product["overall"]
629	    if type(overall) is not str:
630	        raise TypeError("overall must be a str")
631	    if overall not in _QUALITY_VALUES:
632	        raise ValueError("overall must be 'pass' or 'fail'")
633	
634	    terrain = tuple(layer["quality"] for layer in layers)
635	    substrates = tuple(layer["substrate"] for layer in layers)
636	    recomputed = _overall_verdict(crosspoint_result, terrain, substrates)
637	    if overall != recomputed:
638	        raise ValueError(
639	            "overall is inconsistent with crosspoint, layers and substrate"
640	        )
641	
642	    try:
643	        text = json.dumps(
644	            _to_jsonable(product),
645	            ensure_ascii=False,
646	            separators=(",", ":"),
647	            allow_nan=False,
648	        )
649	        return text.encode("utf-8")
650	    except (TypeError, ValueError, UnicodeError) as exc:
651	        raise ValueError(
652	            f"product: could not be serialized to JSON: {exc}"
653	        ) from exc

664	def render(product) -> str:
665	    """Render a :func:`build` result dict as a plain-text report.
666	
667	    ``product`` is first validated with :func:`serialize`, so it must
668	    satisfy that function's full contract; every validation exception
669	    is propagated unchanged and the input is not modified.
670	
671	    On success returns a ``str`` of ``"\\n"``-joined lines with no
672	    trailing newline: an ``OVERALL=<overall>`` line; a
673	    ``CROSSPOINT=`` line with ``count, bias, rmse, max_abs,
674	    within_tolerance, quality`` as semicolon-joined ``key=value``
675	    fields; then, per layer in index order, five lines:
676	    ``LAYER[i]=resolution=<r>;nx=<nx>;ny=<ny>``; ``CELLS[i]=`` with
677	    the layer's ``(count, mean)`` cells in their y-then-x tuple order,
678	    the two values of each cell joined by a comma and the cells joined
679	    by ``|`` (an empty mean renders as ``None``); ``ANALYSIS[i]=`` with
680	    the ``(slope, roughness)`` pairs in the same layout (a missing
681	    slope or roughness renders as ``None``); ``QUALITY[i]=`` with the
682	    fields ``resolution, total, valid, coverage, slope_exceed,
683	    roughness_exceed``; and ``SUBSTRATE[i]=`` with the fields
684	    ``resolution, nx, ny, classes, counts``. ``classes`` is the class
685	    names joined by commas with no spaces; ``counts`` lists
686	    ``unknown, mud, sand, gravel, rock`` in that order joined by
687	    commas. Floats are formatted with ``format(v, ".6f")``, ints in
688	    decimal and ``None`` as ``"None"``.
689	    """
690	    serialize(product)
691	
692	    lines = [f"OVERALL={product['overall']}"]
693	
694	    crosspoint = product["crosspoint"]
695	    cp_fields = ";".join(
696	        f"{key}={_format_scalar(crosspoint[key])}" for key in _CROSSPOINT_KEYS
697	    )
698	    lines.append(f"CROSSPOINT={cp_fields}")
699	
700	    for i, layer in enumerate(product["layers"]):
701	        lines.append(
702	            f"LAYER[{i}]=resolution={format(layer['resolution'], '.6f')}"
703	            f";nx={layer['nx']};ny={layer['ny']}"
704	        )
705	
706	        cell_fields = "|".join(
707	            f"{count},{_format_scalar(mean)}"
708	            for count, mean in layer["cells"]
709	        )
710	        lines.append(f"CELLS[{i}]={cell_fields}")
711	
712	        analysis_fields = "|".join(
713	            f"{_format_scalar(slope)},{_format_scalar(roughness)}"
714	            for slope, roughness in layer["analysis"]
715	        )
716	        lines.append(f"ANALYSIS[{i}]={analysis_fields}")
717	
718	        quality = layer["quality"]
719	        quality_fields = ";".join(
720	            f"{key}={_format_scalar(quality[key])}" for key in _QUALITY_KEYS
721	        )
722	        lines.append(f"QUALITY[{i}]={quality_fields}")
723	
724	        substrate = layer["substrate"]
725	        substrate_fields = ";".join(
726	            (
727	                f"resolution={format(substrate['resolution'], '.6f')}",
728	                f"nx={substrate['nx']}",
729	                f"ny={substrate['ny']}",
730	                f"classes={','.join(substrate['classes'])}",
731	                "counts="
732	                + ",".join(
733	                    str(substrate["counts"][name]) for name in _COUNT_KEYS
734	                ),
735	            )
736	        )
737	        lines.append(f"SUBSTRATE[{i}]={substrate_fields}")
738	
739	    return "\n".join(lines)

815	def load(path):
816	    """Load a :func:`serialize`-produced JSON product from ``path``.
817	
818	    ``path`` must be a non-empty ``str``: a non-str raises
819	    ``TypeError`` and an empty ``str`` raises ``ValueError``. The file
820	    is opened in binary mode (``"rb"``) and read in full; a missing
821	    file raises ``FileNotFoundError``, a directory raises
822	    ``IsADirectoryError`` and every other ``OSError`` is propagated
823	    unchanged. The file is not modified.
824	
825	    The bytes must be exactly those produced by :func:`serialize` for
826	    the same value: compact UTF-8 JSON with no BOM and no trailing
827	    newline. A BOM, a trailing newline, a UTF-8 decoding failure, a
828	    JSON parsing failure or a ``NaN``/``Infinity`` constant raises
829	    ``ValueError``. The decoded value must satisfy the full
830	    :func:`serialize` contract — top-level key order
831	    ``crosspoint, layers, overall`` and all nested key orders, tuple
832	    lengths, field types/ranges and consistency (including ``counts``
833	    matching ``classes`` and an ``overall`` consistent with the
834	    recomputed verdict) — and the file bytes must equal the canonical
835	    re-serialization of the decoded value byte for byte; any
836	    key-order, type, range, consistency or normalization-byte mismatch
837	    raises ``ValueError``.
838	
839	    JSON arrays are recursively converted to tuples and floats are
840	    rounded with ``round(float(v), 6)`` with negative zero normalized
841	    to ``0.0``, mirroring :func:`serialize`.
842	
843	    Returns the product as a dict with keys in the order
844	    ``crosspoint, layers, overall``.
845	    """
846	    if not isinstance(path, str):
847	        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
848	    if path == "":
849	        raise ValueError("path must not be empty")
850	
851	    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
852	        data = handle.read()
853	
854	    if data.startswith(b"\xef\xbb\xbf"):
855	        raise ValueError("file must not start with a UTF-8 BOM")
856	    if data.endswith(b"\n"):
857	        raise ValueError("file must not end with a trailing newline")
858	
859	    try:
860	        text = data.decode("utf-8")
861	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
862	        raise ValueError(f"file is not valid UTF-8: {exc}") from exc
863	
864	    try:
865	        parsed = json.loads(text, parse_constant=_reject_json_constant)
866	    except ValueError as exc:
867	        raise ValueError(f"file is not valid JSON: {exc}") from exc
868	
869	    product = _from_jsonable(parsed)
870	    try:
871	        canonical = serialize(product)
872	    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
873	        raise ValueError(f"file does not contain a valid product: {exc}") from exc
874	
875	    if data != canonical:
876	        raise ValueError(
877	            "file bytes do not match the canonical serialize output"
878	        )
879	
880	    return product

883	def quality_report(path) -> bytes:
884	    """Summarize a :func:`serialize`-produced JSON product as quality bytes.
885	
886	    Exactly one call to :func:`load` is made with ``path`` unchanged and
887	    no other work happens before it; the ``path`` validation contract,
888	    the read behavior, every exception (propagated unchanged) and the
889	    file invariance of :func:`load` therefore apply here verbatim. The
890	    product file is not modified.
891	
892	    Let ``P`` be the dict returned by that single :func:`load` call.
893	    The report is computed from ``P`` alone, without modifying it, and
894	    encoded with keys exactly in the order ``layers, total, valid,
895	    coverage, terrain_exceed, unknown, worst, crosspoint, quality``:
896	
897	    - ``layers``: the number of layers, ``len(P["layers"])``.
898	    - ``total``/``valid``: the sums of ``quality.total`` and
899	      ``quality.valid`` over all layers.
900	    - ``coverage``: ``round(float(valid / total), 6)``.
901	    - ``terrain_exceed``: the sum of ``quality.slope_exceed`` and
902	      ``quality.roughness_exceed`` over all layers.
903	    - ``unknown``: the sum of ``substrate.counts.unknown`` over all
904	      layers.
905	    - ``worst``: the index of the layer maximizing the unrounded tuple
906	      ``(layer unknown, layer slope_exceed + roughness_exceed,
907	      -layer coverage, -index)``.
908	    - ``crosspoint``: ``P["crosspoint"]["quality"]``.
909	    - ``quality``: ``P["overall"]``.
910	
911	    All counts and ``worst`` are ``int`` and ``coverage`` is a
912	    ``float``. The JSON byte specification follows :func:`serialize`:
913	    UTF-8, ``ensure_ascii=False``, ``separators=(",", ":")``,
914	    ``allow_nan=False``, no indentation, no BOM and no trailing
915	    newline; floats are rounded with ``round(float(v), 6)`` and
916	    negative zero is normalized to ``0.0``. Any JSON or UTF-8 encoding
917	    failure raises ``ValueError``.
918	
919	    Returns the JSON document as ``bytes``.
920	    """
921	    product = load(path)
922	
923	    layers = product["layers"]
924	    total = 0
925	    valid = 0
926	    terrain_exceed = 0
927	    unknown = 0
928	    worst = 0
929	    worst_key = None
930	    for i in range(len(layers)):
931	        quality = layers[i]["quality"]
932	        total += quality["total"]
933	        valid += quality["valid"]
934	        exceed = quality["slope_exceed"] + quality["roughness_exceed"]
935	        terrain_exceed += exceed
936	        layer_unknown = layers[i]["substrate"]["counts"]["unknown"]
937	        unknown += layer_unknown
938	        key = (layer_unknown, exceed, -quality["coverage"], -i)
939	        if worst_key is None or key > worst_key:
940	            worst_key = key
941	            worst = i
942	
943	    report = {
944	        "layers": len(layers),
945	        "total": total,
946	        "valid": valid,
947	        "coverage": round(float(valid / total), 6),
948	        "terrain_exceed": terrain_exceed,
949	        "unknown": unknown,
950	        "worst": worst,
951	        "crosspoint": product["crosspoint"]["quality"],
952	        "quality": product["overall"],
953	    }
954	
955	    return _dump_quality_report(report)
